correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all-parameter radial disintegration: endpoint Y on boundary has normalized cone-volume law, independently R_t^d uniform on [t^d,1]. A limit barycenter lies on boundary precisely when its constituent points share a supporting exposed face; boundary a.e. unique outer normal and positive cone density imply positive probability only for common facets. Their supporting hyperplane protects the entire convex hull from int(tK) for each thickness, while an interior endpoint barycenter forces violation eventually. Dominated convergence proves L_q=sum_F p_F^q for every fixed q>=2. Finite measure eta=sum_F p_F^2 delta_{p_F} has moments L_{j+2}; uniqueness on [0,1] recovers each positive weight and multiplicity. Pyramidal simplex weights and parallelotope opposite-facet weights yield quoted sharp anchor bounds. Finite polygon-shell Monte Carlo file verifies only planar q=2 cases; it does not prove arbitrary q/d.

originality.rationale: The higher Beer/k-index literature supplies the definition and inequalities but not a homothetic thin-shell limit. Henk–Linke supply cone-volume facet masses, not a sampled hull-avoidance asymptotic; Beer 1974 treats OUTER parallel-body thickening. Their union does not directly imply the almost-everywhere same-facet event or full inverse moment spectrum without the independent boundary coupling proof. No stronger covering statement identified; indexed searches are not a novelty certificate.
residual_risks: An unindexed geometric-probability paper may formulate the same homothetic thin-shell visibility limit using a different term.
Moment inversion is a standard Hausdorff theorem; originality and value concern its exact facet visibility connection, not moment uniqueness itself.
No convergence rate or simultaneous limit q->infinity established.

value.rationale: This gives a natural all-order geometric-probability asymptotic for all compact convex bodies, distinguishes existence of facets, and recovers with multiplicities an intrinsic anchored facet cone-volume spectrum; it does not claim complete shape reconstruction. The sharp simplex/parallelotope anchor laws further characterize natural extremal configurations.
